title: Waiting for the retest took an NQ breakout from +80% to +8% and doubled the drawdown
author: person-person12
selftext:
Every breakout video says the same thing. Dont chase the candle that breaks the level, wait for price to come back to it and get in there instead. Cleaner entry and a tighter stop. I've heard it for years and I believed it, so I finally ran both versions against each other.

Same rules on both sides. NQ, 15 minute candles, January 2021 to the end of September 2026, one contract, 100k account. Long when a candle closes above the highest high of the previous 20 candles, stop 1.5 ATR below the entry, target 3 ATR above it, flat by the close. The history I test on in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) covers that whole window at 15m, so both versions walked the identical 135,099 candles with commission and slippage charged on entry and exit.

The only difference is the entry. One version buys the candle that breaks the level. The other waits for price to come back, touch that level and close above it, and gives up on the idea if it hasnt happened within 12 candles.

**Enter on the break:** 1,200 trades, 45.4% wins, **+80.3%**, max drawdown 17.5%

**Wait for the retest:** 586 trades, 45.6% wins, **+8.2%**, max drawdown 32.6%

**-----**

The win rate is the part I didnt expect. 45.4 against 45.6 is the same number for all practical purposes, so waiting for the retest did nothing at all for the quality of the trades. It just removed a bit over half of them.

Which half it removed is the whole story. Sorting every trade by how it ended:

Enter on the break, 233 of 1,200 reached the target, 19.4%

Wait for the retest, 81 of 586 reached the target, 13.8%

The losers stopped out at almost the same rate either way, 44.7% against 42.8%. What the retest rule took away was the trades that **ran**. A level that breaks and never comes back to it is the one that was actually going somewhere, and thats exactly the trade youre standing aside for while you wait to be filled at a nicer price.

The drawdown moving the wrong way on the version that trades less than half as often was the other one I had to go back and check. A profit factor of 1.02 means it took in about a dollar and two cents for every dollar it handed back, which is flat. Flat still has losing stretches of six and eight weeks in it, theres just nothing arriving to pay for them.

Its a bit like waiting to merge until theres a gap youre completely comfortable with. You avoid a few hairy merges that way. You also sit on the on-ramp watching the traffic you were trying to join drive off without you.

**\_\_\_\_**

The fair part, because id want this said if it was my strategy on the table. This is one entry rule, one market, one candle size, one window, long only. A retest that counts a wick through the level instead of a close above it is a different test. So is one that lets the level stay alive longer than 12 candles, and so is a retest of a daily level or a prior session high instead of a plain 20 candle high, which is a much more meaningful line than the one I used. I havent run those.

On this one, the retest version kept nearly all of the losers and gave up 152 of the 233 winners that were sitting there.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good that you list what the test doesn't cover. A cleaner way to separate the entry effect from the filtering effect is to look at the 614 trades the break version took that the retest never got, and the 586 they share: do the shared trades perform the same under both entries? That shows how much of the gap is just missed runners. I'd also split by year and by news days, since a long-only NQ breakout leans on a few strong trends, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for tagging them.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
Thats the right split and I hadnt thought of running it that way. **The 586 shared trades under both entries is the clean test**, because if those come out the same then the whole gap is the 614 the retest never got filled on and the entry rule itself is doing nothing.

Year by year I can do. News days I cant tag honestly without a release calendar lined up to the candles, so Id rather leave that out than half do it.

Ill run the shared set and put the numbers up.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Sounds good, thanks for running it. I'll leave it there.
